items.title: 6.7.1 Relation between enthalpy change and calorie content

source_refs.note: Topic 6.7.1, printed pages 126-127 (the print repeats this page). The print's sign on the final value ('-3.72') is given as a positive content.

blocks.text: The enthalpy of combustion of a food, delta Hc, is its calorie content when converted into kilocalories per gram. For glucose, C6H12O6(s) + 6O2(g) gives 6CO2(g) + 6H2O(l), delta H = -2803 kJ per mol. First find delta H per gram: the molar mass of glucose is 180 g per mol, so one mole (180.0 g) burns to give 2803 kJ and 1.0 g gives 2803 / 180 = 15.57 kJ per g. Using delta H (kJ per g) = -4.184 x calorie content, the calorie content = -delta H / 4.184 = 15.57 / 4.184 = 3.72 kcal per g.

blocks.title: Remember
blocks.text: The calories taken in from food must be balanced by working, exercising and positive activity; otherwise the body's growth and maintenance are unbalanced (energy intake against energy expenditure).

blocks.prompt: The enthalpy of combustion of ethanol is -1368 kJ per mol (molar mass 46). What is its calorie content in kcal per g?
blocks.explanation: Per gram: 1368 / 46 = 29.7 kJ per g. In kilocalories: 29.7 / 4.184 = 7.1 kcal per g, nearly twice that of glucose.

items: Calorie content = enthalpy of combustion per gram divided by 4.184 kJ per kcal; glucose: 2803 kJ per mol, 15.57 kJ per g, 3.72 kcal per g; intake should balance expenditure.
